results.name: BG Umbrella Fund PLC
results.strategy_description:
- BG Fund is a multi-strategy event-driven and arbitrage fund.

- The investment team applies an approach which combines robust fundamental analysis with deep technical expertise across financial instruments.

- The strategy aims to be long volatility, positive convexity at all times and with most investments structured with minimal beta.

- The fund is predominantly focused on Europe and operates across asset classes (equity, credit and volatility).

- Investments are rigorously screened to focus on events, catalysts and arbitrage opportunities.

- Capital is allocated by the Investment Committee to the best available ideas, driven by the corporate cycle, market conditions and mispricing opportunities.

- Combining deep analysis with strong risk management and trading expertise, BG Fund’s hedged, convex risk profile differentiates by delivering idiosyncratic and uncorrelated returns.

- The strategy was launched in March 2003 and has more than 20 years of continuous track record.

- Since inception the strategy has delivered attractive risk adjusted returns and performance that has very low correlation to equities and bonds with close to zero beta.

results.strategy_description:
Capstone Alternative Risk Strategy Master (Cayman) LP (the “Fund” or “CARS”) launched in October
2022, and is managed by Jason Goldberg, Senior Portfolio Manager. CARS is a non-correlated strategy
designed to take advantage of the supply/demand imbalance that is created by the mismatch between
strong retail structured products issuance and declining dealer risk appetite. CARS is an extension of
Capstone’s pedigreed experience within risk recycling as we have provided institutional investors
access to the space since 2014. Regarding the opportunity set, the search for yield amongst retail investors has left dealers with increasing volumes of structured product issuance to the retail market. However, the amount of risk that the banks can warehouse has been dramatically curtailed due to regulatory changes after 2008, requiring these dealers to offload more of that risk. Capstone’s expertise in valuing and trading derivatives, and the team’s deep and trusted relationships with structured products desks, allow us to be well placed in partnering with the banks to hedge these products and assume some of that risk in their place. Thanks to the investment team’s experience analyzing, structuring and managing complex derivatives, the strong relationships that Capstone has established with counterparties and the size and scale of our infrastructure, Capstone offers a rich potential source of alpha that, we believe, will be difficult for peers to replicate in the risk recycling space.

results.strategy_description:
Capstone Global Master (Cayman) Limited (“CGM” or the “Fund”) is a multi-strategy fund focused on
trading derivatives across every asset class and region. Since its inception in 2007, the Fund has sought
to generate returns in all market environments, and investors typically view CGM as a portfolio diversifier
given its historically low correlation to equities and other hedge fund strategies.

CGM’s unique alpha comes from Capstone’s understanding of the behavioral biases, structural
inefficiencies, and supply/demand imbalances that persist in derivatives markets. The Fund combines a
diverse set of relative value, volatility, and complementary trading strategies, which are grouped into
four key pillars: Equity Volatility; Equity, Events & Arbitrage; Fixed Income, Currency & Commodities; and
Multi-Asset.

CGM's Investment Committee is constantly looking to ensure that CGM maintains a balance of risk-on
and risk-off strategies, and a limited exposure to the market's direction or volatility. While the
opportunity set tends to be richer in higher volatility environments due to more mispricing in
the derivatives markets, the Fund is designed to be agnostic to the overall level of market volatility.

results.name: Cevian Capital II
results.strategy_description:
The Fund is designed to produce outsized absolute returns whilst limiting permanent loss of capital.

It seeks to accomplish this by taking advantage of the irrational and increasingly short-term behaviors seen in listed equity markets in Europe by itself being a focused, long-term investor with an active ownership approach.

Cevian targets companies that have each of three main characteristics:

Attractive on an “as-is” basis – deeply undervalued and fundamentally attractive companies. Typically, blue-chip names with businesses that exhibit positive long-term dynamics but are not performing at their full potential.

Broad value-creation potential – diverse set of levers designed to drive fundamental improvements across operations, governance and sustainability, structure/strategy and financial (balance sheet). 

Positive influence dynamics – Conviction that, by drawing on existing experience, networks and relationships, we will be able to implement our value-creation initiatives in a hands-on, constructive manner.

Cevian uses rigorous fundamental research, and draws on its significant historical experience in implementing operational improvement programs at past portfolio companies, to identify opportunities to create significant value by implementing broad based value-creation plans across four key areas:

(i)	operational improvements;
(ii)	corporate restructuring and strategic re-orientation; 
(iii)	balance-sheet improvements; and
(iv)	governance and sustainability improvements.

Cevian targets companies that are out of favor, overlooked or misunderstood by the market, yet at the core, have fundamentally strong businesses that are underperforming their potential. These companies are often those that have been negatively impacted by ineffective business strategies, and incoherent or unwieldy corporate structures. 

They may also be cyclically out of favor with more short-term focused investors.

Cevian’s engagement most often leads to direct representation on the target company’s Board of Directors, or indirect representation by catalyzing the appointment to the Board individuals who are not Cevian professionals, but have worked and, in Cevian’s opinion, excelled alongside Cevian in board rooms in the past.

Domain expert PMs (internal employees) manage sleeves directly within set rules. The sleeves are combined along with a risk sleeve which minimizes residual beta and lessens common factor risk.

Diametric's strategy is composed of twelve equity oriented sleeves across fundamental, arbitrage, quant, and other strategy buckets.

Discovery Capital Management is a global investment firm founded in 1999, with a 25+ year track record. As of December 31, 2025, the Fund has delivered annualized net returns of ~37% over 1 year, ~46% over 3 years, 21% over 5 years, and 13% inception to date.  
The firm invests opportunistically across asset classes—including equities, credit, currencies, rates, and commodities—in both emerging and developed markets, using a dynamic long/short approach. 
Led by founder and CIO Robert Citrone, who serves as the firm’s primary risk taker, Discovery Capital combines a top-down macroeconomic framework with deep, bottom-up fundamental analysis. Macro insights help shape the firm’s broad positioning, identifying structural trends, regional dislocations, and policy shifts, while fundamental research drives security selection and theme development at the company and sector level. This integrated process allows Discovery to construct a high-conviction portfolio that reflects both a strategic understanding of global markets and a granular view of individual investment opportunities. 
The firm allocates capital to its highest-conviction ideas and maintains concentrated exposures in key themes and single-name positions. This approach is supported by a deeply experienced investment team, with professionals averaging over 12 years at the firm—bringing continuity, discipline, and a shared investment philosophy that enhances both idea generation and execution.

results.name: ELEVA Absolute Return Dynamic
results.strategy_description: The investment talent and expertise of Eric Bendahan and his team is applied to a bottom-up stock picking approach, which is active in nature and conviction-based in its stock selection. ELEVA Absolute Return Dynamic is aimed at investors with a medium-term horizon. Bottom-up approach: stock-picking is central to the approach and is expected to be the main source of alpha generation over time. This approach is supported by a solid macro view especially during more challenging periods. Great consideration is given to direct and regular contact with companies through on-site company visits and meetings with management. Conviction-based, active stock-picking: the investment strategy is totally active with investment decisions founded on strong convictions. As such, allocations are mostly the result of stock-picking and can deviate meaningfully from the benchmark. However, the Fund Manager is “risk conscious” and tries to maintain a balanced portfolio in terms of risk/reward profile. Style-agnostic: The Sub-Fund is style-agnostic in the sense that investments can be done according to value and/or growth criteria depending on market cycle, visibility, and the manager’s assessment of the relative opportunity set. All cap-approach: The Sub-Fund invests in all market capitalization segments providing sufficient liquidity. Time horizon: When selecting individual stocks, the Fund manager has an 18-24 month investment horizon, over which the target price is set. ESG integration: The strategy is active from an ESG standpoint with the application of exclusions, of ESG analysis and selectivity in the long book, and of active ownership. ELEVA Absolute Return Europe follows a disciplined investment process leveraging ELEVA Capital’s skills and expertise in European Equities with a natural extension of the current successful approach with ELEVA Absolute Return Europe.

Total return is computed using a time-weighted methodology whereby the returns for individual accounting periods are geometrically linked and pro-forma incentive allocations are taken into account. Fred Alger Management, LLC has changed its methodology as of May 31, 2019 for classifying long put positions as short positions. Previously, such option positions had been treated as long positions. For purposes of calculating Exposure, an option's delta adjusted exposure will be used. Delta adjusted exposure represents the expected amount an option price will change if an option's underlying reference security changed by $1. The formula for calculating delta adjusted exposure is the number option contracts multiplied by 100 (option multiplier) and multiplied by both the underlying security price and the option's delta (ranges from -1 to 0 for put options and 0 to 1 for call options based on whether option is in-or out of-the-money). Alpha measures the difference between a portfolio's actual returns and its expected performance, given its level of risk (as measured by beta). Beta measures a portfolio's sensitivity to market movements relative to a particular index; a portfolio with a beta of 1.00 would be expected to have returns equal to such index. R-Squared reflects the percentage of a portfolio's movements that can be explained by movements in its benchmark. Sharpe Ratio was calculated as the portfolio's rate of return less the 3 month T-Bill's rate of return relative to the portfolio's standard deviation less the 3 month T-Bill's standard deviation for the period. Please note that using different points of comparison may have materially different results. Standard Deviation measures how much the portfolio's return has deviated from its average historical return. Upside Capture Ratio and Downside Capture Ratio measure a portfolio's performance in up and down markets, respectively, relative to the benchmark. They are calculated by taking the portfolio's upside (or downside) return and dividing it by the benchmark's upside (or downside) return. A down-market is defined as those time periods in which market return is less than 0.Maximum drawdown is the maximum observed loss from a peak to a trough of a portfolio, before a new peak is attained. Maximum drawdown is an indicator of downside risk over a specified time period. Contribution to Return (CR) is an approximate measure of the contribution by an individual position to the overall portfolio return of the stated period. A daily contribution for each position is calculated by multiplying the position's daily ending position weight by its daily total return. The daily total return is determined by summing the end of day stock price and any dividends and dividing the result by the beginning stock price. These daily contributions are then geometrically linked to determine the CR for the entire stated period. CRs for individual positions are then aggregated by GICS sector.

results.strategy_description:
FIRVO seeks to produce consistent, positive returns throughout varying market cycles while delivering uncorrelated returns to broader market segments. The team pursues opportunities in developed markets, primarily the United States, United Kingdom, Europe and developed Asia, by utilizing proprietary analysis and market research to identify opportunities that may arise from supply and demand imbalances in sovereign bonds, anomalies between market segments such as interest rate futures, cash bonds and interest rate swaps, and diverging interest rate policies across central banks.

Portfolio construction may employ both relative value and directional strategies, with typical trading themes being long/short in nature, with duration hedged to isolate the idiosyncratic or secular exposure desired. The process of isolating the desired exposure makes extensive use of levered interest rates and other derivatives, as well as repurchase agreements. Since its inception, FIRVO has had a strong liquidity management orientation and an overall risk profile that reflects a long liquidity, long volatility, and long event risk bias.

FIRVO’s trading strategies consist primarily of:

•	Basis (futures versus nearby cash securities)

•	Specific security rich/cheap

•	Directional swap spreads and swap spread curve

•	Basis swaps (tenor basis, cross currency basis)

•	Inflation (asset swaps, break-evens, real yields)

•	Volatility (swaptions, options on futures, caps/floors)

•	U.S. Agency Mortgage Backed Securities and Scandinavian Covered Bonds

The Highbridge Tactical Credit Fund ("TCF" or the "Fund") is a multi-strategy hedge fund that focuses on relative value, credit, and volatility strategies. The Fund seeks to generate attractive absolute returns while minimizing equity and credit market sensitivity, constraining volatility, and limiting interest rate exposure (target duration of zero). TCF aims to maintain a stable return path and limit drawdowns, particularly during market stress, with a goal of achieving long-term NAV appreciation.

The investment team, leveraging Highbridge’s proprietary data, technology, and diverse skillset, identifies and aims to profit from relative value opportunities, volatility trading, and idiosyncratic return sources across multiple asset classes. The portfolio is organized into eight Strategy Groups, to augment portfolio construction and risk management. The flexibility to pursue these Strategy Groups, which contain numerous Investment Types, enhances the strategy’s ability to perform throughout market environments.
